16:17 Local Time, 11:17 GMT, 16:47 IST: The umpires get together to assess the light, and they don't look particularly happy with what they are seeing. And there you have it! Play has been halted due to bad light. It's not the end of the day's play just yet, but it's going to be really difficult for the light to improve enough for action to resume today. The three umpires are out in the middle, having a discussion.

16:29 Local Time, 11:29 GMT, 16:59 IST: With the light deteriorating this late in the day, a resumption always looked unlikely after play was halted. Both sides will have their positives to take from the day, although Sri Lanka are likely to be the more pleased of the two. Every Pakistan batter got a start, but none managed to convert it into a substantial score. After being asked to bat, Pakistan made a brisk start through Azan Awais (30) and Tayyab Arif (57 off 51), who put together 86 runs in just 16 overs. Mohammad Taha (51) and Babar Azam (50 off 58) followed with half-centuries of their own, but neither could carry on to make a bigger contribution. Saud Shakeel has looked the most assured at the crease, and Pakistan will be banking on him to make the most of his start and push towards a hundred.

Sri Lanka, meanwhile, kept their faith in the seamers, using spin for just four overs across the day. The pitch offered enough assistance for the quicks to remain in the attack, with Asitha Fernando leading the way with two wickets. Dilshan Madushanka and Milan Priyanath Rathnayake also picked up a wicket apiece. With the fast bowlers doing most of the work, the visitors struggled to keep up with the over rate, managing just 67.2 overs on the day. They will hope to improve on that, but their bigger priority will be to wrap up the remaining five Pakistan wickets as quickly as possible. But for now, that's it from us. We will e-see you tomorrow. Goodbye and good night!
